interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: Department of Pharmaceuticals scheme pages, official guidelines, amendments, FAQs, portals and official call notices only; third-party claims are excluded.

supportingSources.anchor: PRIP guidelines dated 1 October 2025: Component A, NIPER Centres of Excellence, collaboration, priority areas, milestones and reporting
Official PRIP portal for current CoE and collaboration routes

records.sourceAnchor: PRIP Department page and 1 October 2025 guidelines: Component A and NIPER CoE route
observations: Component A is institute and Centre-of-Excellence support at NIPERs, not an unrestricted startup grant.
A startup or company generally reaches this route through an approved NIPER, academic or industry-collaboration arrangement; independent company eligibility must not be inferred.

The PRIP programme period and component outlay are programme-level values, not an applicant entitlement. Priority area, CoE scope, project ownership, IP, milestones, eligible costs and reporting require route-specific confirmation.
The official portal must be checked for the current CoE or collaboration call before the record is actionable.
reviewFollowUps: Identify each current NIPER CoE and its approved focus areas.
Confirm whether a startup can apply directly or only through a named institutional collaboration route.
Extract current application window, IP/data terms, eligible costs, milestone and access conditions.

supportingSources.anchor: Official Department page linking the Gazette, guidelines and PRIP portal
Current PRIP portal call and two-step early-stage application route
Official portal application entry route

records.sourceAnchor: PRIP guidelines: Component B eligibility, TRL routes, co-funding, financial closure and milestone assistance
observations: Component B covers eligible India-registered companies, LLPs and registered partnerships for Pharma and MedTech R&D; sole proprietorships and one-person/non-profit forms are excluded under the reviewed route.
Early-stage applicants need the required DPIIT startup or Udyam MSME evidence. The project must map to an eligible priority area and the relevant TRL route.

The guidelines require a project-specific account, milestone plan, financial closure and applicant co-funding where applicable. Assistance is released in milestones and is not an unconditional grant or guaranteed award.

The portal describes a second call opening soon and a two-step concept-note/detailed-application process for early-stage applications; the live call notice and deadline were not treated as verified for publication.
Component A and Component B ceilings must remain separate. The total PRIP outlay must never be shown as the applicant's eligible value.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the live call notice, deadline, current form and portal status.
Confirm entity-form exclusions, TRL evidence, strategic-priority treatment, co-funding, IP/data, recovery and milestone rules against the current FAQ and guideline.
Review whether assistance is grant, reimbursement, or another instrument for each route before publishing a benefit label.

records.sourceAnchor: SPI/RPTUAS revised guideline, FAQ and 2026 modification
observations: RPTUAS is for existing Indian pharmaceutical manufacturing units with preceding-three-year average turnover below the stated ceiling and an upgrade scope toward Revised Schedule M and/or WHO-GMP.

The reviewed sources describe turnover bands with 20%, 15% and 10% incentive rates, subject to the current maximum and eligible-investment rules. This is a reimbursement/capital-subsidy route, not a working-capital loan or automatic reimbursement.

Only eligible investment after 1 January 2024 and the prescribed utilities, clean-room, testing, effluent, certification and other approved heads can be counted; the current modification changes the staged certification sequence.

The official annual-report evidence describes an earlier application window and expected sanctioning of remaining outlay by March 2026. No current September 2026 new-intake window was independently verified, so this route remains paused.
Users must not be told that the scheme page alone proves a new application is open.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm current new-application versus pending-project status with the live Department/SIDBI route.
Reconcile the current maximum, turnover treatment, certification sequence, eligible heads, release stages and remaining budget across the 2026 amendment, FAQ and implementation notice.
Keep paused until an official live intake or explicit route for pending applicants is verified.

supportingSources.anchor: Official SMDI scheme page and current calls/modifications
Department notices and SMDI proposal calls

records.sourceAnchor: SMDI Chapter IV: capacity-building and skill-development beneficiaries, course routes and reimbursement
observations: This component primarily supports eligible universities, institutes, courses, students and existing medical-device workforce; it is not a direct unrestricted founder or company grant.
The guideline separates postgraduate-course support from diploma and short-term training routes, with different institutions, batches, cost-sharing and reimbursement limits.

The reviewed guideline describes up to 75% of course cost or INR 21 crore for eligible central-government postgraduate-course institutions, with separate non-recurring and recurring limits; diploma and short-term support is candidate-linked.
The Department lists later modifications and current calls, so the 2024 guideline alone cannot establish a live application route.
reviewFollowUps: Read the latest capacity-building modification and current call notice.
Confirm institution, course, NCVET, batch, candidate, cost-sharing, reimbursement and reporting rules.
Model this as an institutional/training opportunity, not as a company cash benefit.

supportingSources.anchor: Official SMDI scheme page, common-facility route and current proposal notices

records.sourceAnchor: SMDI Chapter II: common and testing facilities, SPV/cluster structure, caps and release conditions
observations: This route is for cluster or institutional common facilities and testing facilities, not a general subsidy for an individual company's ordinary equipment.
The reviewed guideline describes cluster/SPV and institution routes with minimum participating medical-device units and separate public/private assistance percentages and caps.
Common-facility assistance and testing-facility assistance are separate benefits, with asset-use, maintenance, verification and recovery conditions.
The Department's current notices and extensions must control whether a proposal window is open.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current call, deadline and proposal template.
Extract the exact SPV composition, minimum-unit, accreditation, land, O&M, contribution, release and clawback requirements.
Show any cap as project/component-specific and never as an individual founder entitlement.

records.sourceAnchor: SMDI Chapter III: domestic production of medical-device components, raw materials and accessories
observations: Eligible applicants include Indian companies/LLPs, government organisations and qualifying SPVs manufacturing key components, raw materials, accessories or specified finished devices/IVDs that reduce import dependence.

The guideline describes a one-time capital subsidy on reimbursement basis: 20%, 15% or 10% by turnover band, subject to INR 10 crore, with a separate 20%/INR 10 crore rule for central/state government organisations.

The subsidy is computed on eligible fixed investment excluding land and is released only after completion, commissioning, Chartered Engineer and statutory-auditor evidence, first-sales evidence and PMA verification.
The eligible item list can be revised or supplemented through the technical and scheme authorities, so the current call and approved product list must be checked before matching a business.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm the live proposal window, eligible product/component list and current GTE list.
Extract turnover definition, project duration, statutory-clearance, first-sale, audit, O&M and recovery conditions.
Keep the benefit as a post-completion reimbursement subsidy, not upfront working capital.

records.sourceAnchor: SMDI Chapter V: pre-clinical, clinical, post-market and new-IVD evidence routes
observations: The route covers eligible Indian medical-device manufacturers, IVD manufacturers and specified institutes for animal/pre-clinical studies, clinical investigations, post-market clinical follow-up and clinical-performance evaluation of new IVDs.
Manufacturers need the required Indian facility and regulatory/test-licence or study readiness evidence; the grant does not replace ethics, regulatory, safety, consent or clinical obligations.

The guideline describes reimbursement caps by study type: up to INR 1 crore for new-IVD performance evaluation, INR 2 crore for pre-clinical studies, INR 5 crore for clinical investigations and INR 1 crore for post-market follow-up, each also limited by the stated percentage of expenditure.

The Department lists a 2026 modification affecting the operational guideline, so the 2024 text cannot be published as the sole current rule. Clinical data retention and government-access obligations are material fine print.
reviewFollowUps: Apply the 2026 modification to paragraphs 5.4 and 5.11 and reconcile any changed applicant, study, cost or release conditions.
Confirm current call dates, PMA route, device class, statutory/ethics prerequisites, audit evidence and data-retention requirements.
Require specialist reviewer sign-off before publication.

records.sourceAnchor: SMDI Chapter VI: industry bodies, studies, events, databases and market-development activities
observations: The component provides support to recognised industry associations/bodies, experienced study or survey organisations and government/quasi-government agencies; it is not a general company advertising subsidy.
Eligible activities include study reports, seminars, conferences, workshops, exhibitions, databases, mega events, international participation and other approved industry-development activities.
The guideline describes competitive or nominated routes, staged grant release for studies, Department ownership/non-commercial-use conditions for funded reports and output verification.
The component outlay is a programme budget, not an individual applicant ceiling. Current calls, eligible activity limits and reporting requirements must be verified from the Department.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm current applicant classes, call, grant limits, procurement and reporting terms.
Keep non-financial logo support distinct from grant-in-aid and from a company marketing benefit.
Verify ownership and permitted-use terms for any funded study or database.

publicationGuard.reason: PRIP, RPTUAS and SMDI contain distinct applicant classes, benefit mechanisms, reimbursement rules, amendments and live-call dependencies. The official sources support structured drafts, but the records require human review before publication or actionable recommendations.
